THE CALL OF AVRAM — CHAPTERS 12 THROUGH 15

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 12 The Call of Avram — Egypt

12:1 Now YHWH said to Avram: Go from your country, and from your kindred, and from your father's house, to the land that I will show you.

12:2 And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing.

12:3 And I will bless those who bless you, and him who curses you I will curse; and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

12:4 So Avram went, as YHWH had spoken to him; and Lot went with him; and Avram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Charan.

12:5 And Avram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all their possessions that they had gathered, and the souls that they had acquired in Charan; and they went forth to go to the land of Kena'an; and to the land of Kena'an they came.

12:6 And Avram passed through the land to the place of Shekhem, to the terebinth of Moreh. And the Kena'ani was then in the land.

12:7 And YHWH appeared to Avram, and said: To your descendants I will give this land; and he built there an altar to YHWH, who had appeared to him.

12:8 And he moved from there to the mountain east of Beit-El, and pitched his tent, with Beit-El on the west and Ai on the east; and he built there an altar to YHWH, and called upon the name of YHWH.

12:9 And Avram journeyed, going on still toward the South.

12:10 And there was a famine in the land; and Avram went down to Mitzrayim to sojourn there, for the famine was severe in the land.

12:11 And it came to pass, when he had come near to enter Mitzrayim, that he said to Sarai his wife: Behold now, I know that you are a woman fair to look upon.

12:12 And it will come to pass, when the Egyptians see you, that they will say: This is his wife; and they will kill me, but you they will keep alive.

12:13 Say, please, that you are my sister; that it may be well with me for your sake, and that my life may be spared because of you.

12:14 And it came to pass, when Avram had come into Mitzrayim, that the Egyptians saw the woman, that she was very fair.

12:15 And the officials of Pharaoh saw her, and praised her to Pharaoh; and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.

12:16 And he dealt well with Avram for her sake; and he had sheep, and oxen, and donkeys, and menservants, and maidservants, and she-donkeys, and camels.

12:17 And YHWH plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Avram's wife.

12:18 And Pharaoh called Avram, and said: What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?

12:19 Why did you say, She is my sister, so that I took her to be my wife? Now therefore, behold your wife; take her, and go your way.

12:20 And Pharaoh gave men charge concerning him; and they sent him away, and his wife, and all that he had.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] A genuinely new, substantial witness surfaces here: 1QapGen ar (the Genesis Apocryphon), an Aramaic 'Rewritten Scripture' text whose best-preserved columns retell precisely this narrative (Avram's journey, the Egypt/Sarai episode) and continue into the war of the kings (ch.14). Genre-disclosed: an embellished, first-person retelling, not a running-text witness to the Hebrew biblical text -- consistent with the standing genre-disclosure rule already applied to 4Q252 and the Reworked Pentateuch texts. Not treated as manuscript evidence for MT, but flagged for the book-level census given its direct, sustained thematic overlap with chapters 12-15. No witness in the standing running-text census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The chapter uses יהוה exclusively throughout (vv.1,4,7,8,17), continuing to alternate with the אלהים-dominant chapters already logged in Part One, now confirmed as a book-wide pattern rather than one confined to the primeval history. No new translator-decision cruxes beyond standard proper-name transliteration.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 13 Avram and Lot Separate

13:1 And Avram went up out of Mitzrayim, he, and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the South.

13:2 And Avram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.

13:3 And he went on his journeys from the South even to Beit-El, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Beit-El and Ai;

13:4 to the place of the altar which he had made there at first; and Avram called there on the name of YHWH.

13:5 And Lot also, who went with Avram, had flocks, and herds, and tents.

13:6 And the land was not able to bear them, that they might dwell together; for their possessions were great, so that they could not dwell together.

13:7 And there was strife between the herdsmen of Avram's cattle and the herdsmen of Lot's cattle. And the Kena'ani and the Perizzi dwelt then in the land.

13:8 And Avram said to Lot: Let there be no strife, please, between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen; for we are brothers.

13:9 Is not the whole land before you? Please separate yourself from me; if you take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if you take the right hand, then I will go to the left.

13:10 And Lot lifted up his eyes, and saw all the plain of the Yarden, that it was well watered everywhere, before YHWH destroyed Sedom and Amorah, like the garden of YHWH, like the land of Mitzrayim, as you go to Tzo'ar.

13:11 So Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Yarden; and Lot journeyed east; and they separated themselves, one from the other.

13:12 Avram dwelt in the land of Kena'an, and Lot dwelt in the cities of the plain, and moved his tent as far as Sedom.

13:13 Now the men of Sedom were wicked and sinners against YHWH exceedingly.

13:14 And YHWH said to Avram, after Lot had separated from him: Lift up now your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward;

13:15 for all the land which you see, to you I will give it, and to your descendants forever.

13:16 And I will make your descendants as the dust of the earth; so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then your descendants also can be numbered.

13:17 Arise, walk through the land, in its length and in its breadth; for I will give it to you.

13:18 And Avram moved his tent, and came and dwelt by the terebinths of Mamre, which are in Chevron, and built there an altar to YHWH.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing running-text census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. 1QapGen's best-preserved narrative columns are documented as concluding with Avram's return to Canaan and the war of the kings (ch.14) -- this chapter's separation narrative falls within that general span, but no specific citation for this chapter's content was located this session; not claimed. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] No new divine-name policy applications beyond the established YHWH rendering; the chapter uses יהוה exclusively (vv.4,10,13,14,18). No new translator-decision cruxes identified.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 14 The War of the Kings — Malki-Tzedek

14:1 And it came to pass in the days of Amrafel king of Shinar, Aryokh king of Elasar, Kedorla'omer king of Eilam, and Tidal king of Goyim,

14:2 that they made war with Bera king of Sedom, and with Birsha king of Amorah, Shinav king of Admah, and Shem'ever king of Tzevoyim, and the king of Bela — that is Tzo'ar.

14:3 All these joined together in the valley of Siddim — that is the Salt Sea.

14:4 Twelve years they had served Kedorla'omer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

14:5 And in the fourteenth year Kedorla'omer came, and the kings who were with him, and struck the Refa'im in Ashterot-Karnayim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Eimim in Shaveh-Kiryatayim,

14:6 and the Chori in their Mount Se'ir, as far as El-Paran, which is by the wilderness.

14:7 And they turned back, and came to Ein-Mishpat — that is Kadesh — and struck all the country of the Amaleki, and also the Emori who dwelt in Chatzatzon-Tamar.

14:8 And the king of Sedom, and the king of Amorah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Tzevoyim, and the king of Bela — that is Tzo'ar — went out, and they joined battle with them in the valley of Siddim,

14:9 with Kedorla'omer king of Eilam, and Tidal king of Goyim, and Amrafel king of Shinar, and Aryokh king of Elasar — four kings against five.

14:10 And the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits; and the kings of Sedom and Amorah fled, and fell there; and those who remained fled to the mountain.

14:11 And they took all the goods of Sedom and Amorah, and all their food, and went their way.

14:12 And they took Lot, Avram's brother's son, who dwelt in Sedom, and his goods, and departed.

14:13 And one who had escaped came and told Avram the Hebrew; for he dwelt by the terebinths of Mamre the Emori, brother of Eshkol and brother of Aner; and these were allies of Avram.

14:14 And when Avram heard that his brother was taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.

14:15 And he divided himself against them by night, he and his servants, and struck them, and pursued them to Chovah, which is on the left hand of Damesek.

14:16 And he brought back all the goods, and also brought back his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.

14:17 And the king of Sedom went out to meet him, after his return from the defeat of Kedorla'omer and the kings who were with him, at the valley of Shaveh — that is the King's Valley.

14:18 And Malki-Tzedek king of Shalem brought forth bread and wine; and he was priest of the Creator Most High.

14:19 And he blessed him, and said: Blessed be Avram of the Creator Most High, possessor of heaven and earth;

14:20 and blessed be the Creator Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand. And he gave him a tenth of everything.

14:21 And the king of Sedom said to Avram: Give me the persons, and take the goods for yourself.

14:22 And Avram said to the king of Sedom: I have lifted up my hand to YHWH, the Creator Most High, possessor of heaven and earth,

14:23 that I will not take a thread nor a sandal strap nor anything that is yours, lest you should say: I have made Avram rich;

14:24 save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me — Aner, Eshkol, and Mamre — let them take their portion.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 1QapGen ar's best-preserved narrative columns are documented as concluding with a retelling of precisely this chapter -- the war of the kings. Genre-disclosed per the standing rule (Section 2.2 of the apparatus): a first-person, embellished Aramaic retelling, not a running-text witness to MT. Not treated as manuscript evidence for the biblical text; flagged as a real, substantial thematic parallel. No witness in the standing running-text census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 18-20 and 22 -- אל עליון ("El Elyon," the Creator Most High) is Malki-Tzedek’s own cultic title, distinct from both plain אלהים and יהוה. Verse 22 is decisive for how this reconstruction renders it: Avram’s own oath explicitly joins the two designations (יהוה אל עליון, "YHWH, the Creator Most High"), the text’s own identification of Malki-Tzedek’s deity with Avram’s. Rendered "the Creator Most High" throughout, preserving "Elyon" as a disclosed, distinct compound title rather than silently flattened to plain "the Creator" -- consistent with the project’s standing practice for El-compounds (Section 3.1 of the apparatus). Malki-Tzedek himself, a non-Israelite Canaanite priest-king, is not otherwise commented on beyond the text’s own description.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 15 The Covenant Between the Pieces

15:1 After these things the word of YHWH came to Avram in a vision, saying: Fear not, Avram, I am your shield; your reward shall be exceedingly great.

15:2 And Avram said: Sovereign YHWH, what will you give me, seeing I go childless, and the heir of my house is Eli'ezer of Dammesek?

15:3 And Avram said: Behold, you have given me no offspring; and one born in my house is my heir.

15:4 And behold, the word of YHWH came to him, saying: This man shall not be your heir; but one who shall come forth from your own body shall be your heir.

15:5 And he brought him outside, and said: Look now toward the heavens, and count the stars, if you are able to count them. And he said to him: So shall your descendants be.

15:6 And he believed in YHWH; and he counted it to him as righteousness.

15:7 And he said to him: I am YHWH who brought you out of Ur Kasdim, to give you this land to inherit it.

15:8 And he said: Sovereign YHWH, how shall I know that I shall inherit it?

15:9 And he said to him: Take for me a heifer three years old, and a female goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.

15:10 And he took all these, and divided them in the middle, and laid each half opposite the other; but the birds he did not divide.

15:11 And when the birds of prey came down upon the carcasses, Avram drove them away.

15:12 And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Avram; and behold, a horror of great darkness fell upon him.

15:13 And he said to Avram: Know for certain that your descendants shall be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

15:14 and also that nation, whom they shall serve, I will judge; and afterward they shall come out with great substance.

15:15 But you shall go to your fathers in peace; you shall be buried in a good old age.

15:16 And in the fourth generation they shall come back here; for the iniquity of the Emori is not yet full.

15:17 And it came to pass, that when the sun went down, and there was thick darkness, behold, a smoking oven, and a flaming torch that passed between these pieces.

15:18 On that day YHWH made a covenant with Avram, saying: To your descendants I have given this land, from the river of Mitzrayim to the great river, the river Perat;

15:19 the Keini, and the Kenizi, and the Kadmoni,

15:20 and the Chiti, and the Perizi, and the Refa'im,

15:21 and the Emori, and the Kena'ani, and the Girgashi, and the Yevusi.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 1QapGen ar's documented coverage (Gen 12-15, per its own colophon-adjacent narrative arc) nominally includes this chapter, but no specific citation for this chapter's content was located this session -- not claimed beyond the general span already disclosed at ch.12 and ch.14. No witness in the standing running-text census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 2 and 8 -- אדני יהוה (Adonai YHWH), a distinct compound construction from the אלהים-apposition and אל עליון constructions already documented (2:4, ch.14) -- traditionally read aloud as "Adonai Elohim" to avoid doubling the spoken title "Adonai," but written as the Tetragrammaton. Rendered "Sovereign YHWH," consistent with the precedent already established for this exact construction at Shemot 23:17. Verse 6's ויחשבה לו צדקה ("and he counted it to him as righteousness") preserves a genuine grammatical ambiguity in the subject of the verb (Avram counting YHWH's word as trustworthy, or YHWH counting Avram's trust as righteousness) -- the majority reading (YHWH as subject) is followed, with the alternative disclosed rather than treated as settled. No number rounded or adjusted in the four-hundred-year/four-generations figures of vv.13,16.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 16 Hagar and Yishma'el

16:1 Now Sarai, Avram's wife, bore him no children; and she had an Egyptian maidservant, whose name was Hagar.

16:2 And Sarai said to Avram: Behold now, YHWH has restrained me from bearing; please go in to my maidservant; it may be that I shall be built up through her. And Avram listened to the voice of Sarai.

16:3 And Sarai, Avram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant, after Avram had dwelt ten years in the land of Kena'an, and gave her to Avram her husband as a wife.

16:4 And he went in to Hagar, and she conceived; and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.

16:5 And Sarai said to Avram: My wrong be upon you; I gave my maidservant into your bosom, and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes; YHWH judge between me and you.

16:6 But Avram said to Sarai: Behold, your maidservant is in your hand; do to her as is good in your eyes. And Sarai dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her presence.

16:7 And the angel of YHWH found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur.

16:8 And he said: Hagar, Sarai's maidservant, where have you come from, and where are you going? And she said: I flee from the presence of my mistress Sarai.

16:9 And the angel of YHWH said to her: Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hands.

16:10 And the angel of YHWH said to her: I will greatly multiply your descendants, that they shall not be numbered for multitude.

16:11 And the angel of YHWH said to her: Behold, you are with child, and shall bear a son; and you shall call his name Yishma'el, because YHWH has heard your affliction.

16:12 And he shall be a wild donkey of a man; his hand against everyone, and everyone's hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers.

16:13 And she called the name of YHWH who spoke to her: You are El Ro'i; for she said, Have I even here seen him who sees me, and lived?

16:14 Therefore the well was called Be'er-Lachai-Ro'i; behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.

16:15 And Hagar bore Avram a son; and Avram called his son's name, whom Hagar bore, Yishma'el.

16:16 And Avram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Yishma'el to Avram.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 7, 9, 10, 11 -- מלאך יהוה ("the angel/messenger of YHWH") -- a genuine, well-documented crux running throughout the Hebrew Bible: whether this figure is a created intermediary distinct from YHWH, a theophanic manifestation, or functionally identified with YHWH itself. The text's own grammar keeps this open -- v.13 has Hagar respond to the malakh's words as though YHWH itself had spoken to her directly, without the text marking a transition. Rendered literally ("the angel of YHWH") without resolving the identity question. Verse 13's אל ראי ("El Ro'i") is retained as a transliterated proper name/title rather than translated, consistent with the project's practice for distinct compound divine titles (cf. אל עליון at ch.14) -- notably the only instance in the Hebrew Bible of a woman naming the deity, and the namer is a non-Israelite (Egyptian) woman; the verse's own explanatory wordplay (ראה, "to see") is preserved in the note rather than the translation.

THE COVENANT OF CIRCUMCISION — CHAPTER 17

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 17 The Covenant of Circumcision — Avraham and Sarah

17:1 And when Avram was ninety-nine years old, YHWH appeared to Avram, and said to him: I am El Shaddai; walk before me, and be blameless.

17:2 And I will make my covenant between me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly.

17:3 And Avram fell on his face; and the Creator talked with him, saying:

17:4 As for me, behold, my covenant is with you, and you shall be a father of a multitude of nations.

17:5 Neither shall your name any more be called Avram, but your name shall be Avraham; for I have made you a father of a multitude of nations.

17:6 And I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come from you.

17:7 And I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be the Creator to you and to your descendants after you.

17:8 And I will give to you, and to your descendants after you, the land of your sojournings, all the land of Kena'an, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their Creator.

17:9 And the Creator said to Avraham: As for you, you shall keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you throughout their generations.

17:10 This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your descendants after you: every male among you shall be circumcised.

17:11 And you shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of a covenant between me and you.

17:12 And he who is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he who is born in the house, or bought with money from any foreigner, who is not of your descendants.

17:13 He who is born in your house, and he who is bought with your money, must be circumcised; and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.

17:14 And the uncircumcised male, who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant.

17:15 And the Creator said to Avraham: As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be.

17:16 And I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her; and I will bless her, and she shall become nations; kings of peoples shall come from her.

17:17 Then Avraham fell on his face, and laughed, and said in his heart: Shall a child be born to him who is a hundred years old? And shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?

17:18 And Avraham said to the Creator: Oh that Yishma'el might live before you!

17:19 And the Creator said: No, but Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Yitzhak; and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.

17:20 And as for Yishma'el, I have heard you; behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.

17:21 But my covenant I will establish with Yitzhak, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this set time next year.

17:22 And he finished talking with him, and the Creator went up from Avraham.

17:23 And Avraham took Yishma'el his son, and all who were born in his house, and all who were bought with his money, every male among the men of Avraham's house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin on that very day, as the Creator had said to him.

17:24 And Avraham was ninety-nine years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

17:25 And Yishma'el his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

17:26 On that very day Avraham was circumcised, and Yishma'el his son.

17:27 And all the men of his house, born in the house, and bought with money from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing census produces a confirmed reading for this chapter. No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 1 -- אל שדי (El Shaddai) -- rendered as a transliterated, distinct compound title rather than translated or flattened to plain "the Creator," consistent with the standing practice for El-compounds (Section 3.1 of the apparatus; cf. אל עליון at ch.14, אל ראי at ch.16). The chapter's central name changes are real, disclosed philological facts, not merely narrative color: אברם (Avram) to אברהם (Avraham) inserts a letter ה (heh); שרי (Sarai) to שרה (Sarah) replaces a final י (yod) with ה (heh). Both name forms are used precisely at their correct point in the narrative (Avram/Sarai before this chapter, Avraham/Sarah from v.5/v.15 onward, per MT's own usage), not retrofitted across earlier chapters. Verses 15-21's repeated distinction between the covenant established with Yitzhak specifically versus Yishma'el's separate (but real, unrevoked) blessing is preserved exactly as the Hebrew presents it, without softening either promise relative to the other.

BERESHIT — CHAPTER 18 The Three Visitors — Intercession for Sedom

18:1 And YHWH appeared to him by the terebinths of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day;

18:2 and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, three men stood by him; and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth,

18:3 and said: My lord, if now I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass by your servant.

18:4 Let now a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree;

18:5 and I will fetch a morsel of bread, and refresh your hearts; after that you shall pass on; since you have come to your servant. And they said: So do, as you have said.

18:6 And Avraham hurried into the tent to Sarah, and said: Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.

18:7 And Avraham ran to the herd, and fetched a calf tender and good, and gave it to the servant; and he hurried to prepare it.

18:8 And he took curds, and milk, and the calf which he had prepared, and set it before them; and he stood by them under the tree, and they ate.

18:9 And they said to him: Where is Sarah your wife? And he said: Behold, in the tent.

18:10 And he said: I will certainly return to you when the season comes around; and behold, Sarah your wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him.

18:11 Now Avraham and Sarah were old, well advanced in age; it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.

18:12 And Sarah laughed within herself, saying: After I am worn out shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?

18:13 And YHWH said to Avraham: Why did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I indeed bear a child, who am old?

18:14 Is anything too hard for YHWH? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes around, and Sarah shall have a son.

18:15 Then Sarah denied it, saying: I did not laugh; for she was afraid. And he said: No, but you did laugh.

18:16 And the men rose up from there, and looked out toward Sedom; and Avraham went with them to bring them on the way.

18:17 And YHWH said: Shall I hide from Avraham that which I am doing;

18:18 seeing that Avraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

18:19 For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of YHWH, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that YHWH may bring upon Avraham that which he has spoken of him.

18:20 And YHWH said: The outcry of Sedom and Amorah is indeed great, and their sin is exceedingly grievous.

18:21 I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the outcry that has come to me; and if not, I will know.

18:22 And the men turned from there, and went toward Sedom; but Avraham still stood before YHWH.

18:23 And Avraham drew near, and said: Will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked?

18:24 Suppose there are fifty righteous within the city; will you indeed sweep it away, and not spare the place for the fifty righteous who are in it?

24:7 YHWH, the Creator of heaven, who took me from my father's house, and from the land of my kindred, and who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, To your descendants I will give this land — he will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.

24:8 And if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you shall be clear from this my oath; only do not bring my son back there.

24:9 And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Avraham his master, and swore to him concerning that matter.

24:10 And the servant took ten camels of his master's camels, and departed, with all kinds of good things of his master's in his hand; and he arose, and went to Aram-Naharayim, to the city of Nachor.

24:11 And he made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water, at the time of evening, the time that women go out to draw water.

24:12 And he said: O YHWH, Creator of my master Avraham, please give me good speed this day, and show kindness to my master Avraham.

24:13 Behold, I stand by the fountain of water; and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

24:14 Let it come to pass, that the young woman to whom I shall say, Let down your pitcher, I pray you, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give your camels drink also — let the same be she that you have appointed for your servant, for Yitzhak; and thereby I shall know that you have shown kindness to my master.

24:15 And it came to pass, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rivkah came out, who was born to Betu'el, son of Milkah, the wife of Nachor, Avraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

24:16 And the young woman was very fair to look upon, a virgin, and no man had known her; and she went down to the fountain, and filled her pitcher, and came up.

24:17 And the servant ran to meet her, and said: Let me, I pray you, drink a little water from your pitcher.

24:18 And she said: Drink, my lord; and she hurried, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.

24:19 And when she had finished giving him drink, she said: I will draw water for your camels also, until they have finished drinking.

24:20 And she hurried, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.

24:21 And the man, gazing at her, remained silent, to know whether YHWH had made his journey prosperous or not.

24:22 And it came to pass, as the camels had finished drinking, that the man took a golden nose ring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands, of ten shekels weight of gold;

24:23 and said: Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father's house for us to lodge?

24:24 And she said to him: I am the daughter of Betu'el, the son of Milkah, whom she bore to Nachor.

24:25 And she said further to him: We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge.

24:26 And the man bowed his head, and worshiped YHWH.

24:27 And he said: Blessed be YHWH, the Creator of my master Avraham, who has not forsaken his kindness and his truth toward my master; as for me, YHWH has led me on the way to the house of my master's brothers.

24:28 And the young woman ran, and told her mother's household about these things.

24:29 And Rivkah had a brother, and his name was Lavan; and Lavan ran out to the man, to the fountain.

24:30 And it came to pass, when he saw the nose ring, and the bracelets upon his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rivkah his sister, saying, This is what the man said to me, that he came to the man; and behold, he stood by the camels at the fountain.

24:31 And he said: Come in, blessed of YHWH; why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.

24:32 And the man came into the house, and he unloaded the camels; and he gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.

24:33 And food was set before him to eat; but he said: I will not eat until I have told my errand. And he said: Speak on.

24:34 And he said: I am Avraham's servant.

24:35 And YHWH has blessed my master greatly; and he has become great; and he has given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and menservants, and maidservants, and camels, and donkeys.

24:36 And Sarah my master's wife bore a son to my master when she was old; and to him he has given all that he has.

24:37 And my master made me swear, saying: You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Kena'ani, in whose land I dwell.

24:38 But you shall go to my father's house, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son.

24:39 And I said to my master: Perhaps the woman will not follow me.

24:40 And he said to me: YHWH, before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and make your journey prosperous; and you shall take a wife for my son from my kindred, and from my father's house;

24:41 then you shall be clear from my oath, when you come to my kindred; and if they do not give her to you, you shall be clear from my oath.

24:42 And I came this day to the fountain, and said: O YHWH, Creator of my master Avraham, if now you do prosper my way which I go —

24:43 behold, I stand by the fountain of water; let it come to pass, that the young woman who comes out to draw water, to whom I shall say, Give me, I pray you, a little water from your pitcher to drink —

24:44 and she shall say to me, Both drink, and I will also draw for your camels — let the same be the woman whom YHWH has appointed for my master's son.

24:45 And before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rivkah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down to the fountain, and drew water; and I said to her: Please let me drink.

24:46 And she hurried, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said: Drink, and I will give your camels drink also; so I drank, and she gave the camels drink also.

24:47 And I asked her, and said: Whose daughter are you? And she said: The daughter of Betu'el, Nachor's son, whom Milkah bore to him; and I put the ring upon her nose, and the bracelets upon her hands.

24:48 And I bowed my head, and worshiped YHWH, and blessed YHWH, the Creator of my master Avraham, who had led me on the right way, to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son.

24:49 And now, if you will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.

24:50 Then Lavan and Betu'el answered, and said: The matter proceeds from YHWH; we cannot speak to you bad or good.

24:51 Behold, Rivkah is before you; take her, and go, and let her be your master's son's wife, as YHWH has spoken.

24:52 And it came to pass, when Avraham's servant heard their words, that he bowed himself to the earth to YHWH.

24:53 And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and garments, and gave them to Rivkah; and he gave precious things also to her brother and to her mother.

24:54 And they ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and stayed all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said: Send me away to my master.

24:55 And her brother and her mother said: Let the young woman stay with us a few days, at least ten; after that she shall go.

24:56 And he said to them: Do not delay me, seeing YHWH has prospered my way; send me away, that I may go to my master.

24:57 And they said: We will call the young woman, and inquire at her mouth.

24:58 And they called Rivkah, and said to her: Will you go with this man? And she said: I will go.

24:59 And they sent away Rivkah their sister, and her nurse, and Avraham's servant, and his men.

24:60 And they blessed Rivkah, and said to her: Our sister, may you become thousands of ten thousands, and let your descendants possess the gate of those who hate them.

24:61 And Rivkah arose, and her young women, and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man; and the servant took Rivkah, and went his way.

24:62 And Yitzhak came from the way of Be'er-Lachai-Ro'i; for he dwelt in the land of the South.

24:63 And Yitzhak went out to meditate in the field toward evening; and he lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold, camels were coming.

24:64 And Rivkah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Yitzhak, she dismounted from the camel.

24:65 And she said to the servant: Who is this man who walks in the field to meet us? And the servant said: It is my master. And she took her veil, and covered herself.

24:66 And the servant told Yitzhak all the things that he had done.

24:67 And Yitzhak brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rivkah, and she became his wife; and he loved her. And Yitzhak was comforted after his mother's death.

25:2 And she bore him Zimran, and Yokshan, and Medan, and Midyan, and Yishbak, and Shuach.

25:8 And Avraham breathed his last, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.

25:9 And Yitzhak and Yishma'el his sons buried him in the cave of Makhpelah, in the field of Efron the son of Tzochar the Chiti, east of Mamre;

25:10 the field which Avraham purchased from the sons of Chet; there Avraham was buried, and Sarah his wife.

25:11 And it came to pass after the death of Avraham, that the Creator blessed Yitzhak his son; and Yitzhak dwelt by Be'er-Lachai-Ro'i.

25:12 Now these are the generations of Yishma'el, Avraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maidservant, bore to Avraham.

25:13 And these are the names of the sons of Yishma'el, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Yishma'el, Nevayot; and Kedar, and Adbe'el, and Mivsam,

25:14 and Mishma, and Dumah, and Masa;

25:15 Chadad, and Teima, Yetur, Nafish, and Kedmah.

25:16 These are the sons of Yishma'el, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments; twelve princes according to their nations.

25:17 And these are the years of the life of Yishma'el: a hundred and thirty-seven years; and he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.

25:18 And they dwelt from Chavilah to Shur, which is before Mitzrayim, as you go toward Ashur; he settled in the presence of all his brothers.

25:19 And these are the generations of Yitzhak, Avraham's son: Avraham begot Yitzhak.

25:20 And Yitzhak was forty years old when he took Rivkah, daughter of Betu'el the Arami of Padan-Aram, sister of Lavan the Arami, as his wife.

25:21 And Yitzhak pleaded with YHWH for his wife, because she was barren; and YHWH let himself be entreated by him, and Rivkah his wife conceived.

25:22 And the children struggled together within her; and she said: If it is so, why do I live? And she went to inquire of YHWH.

25:23 And YHWH said to her: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your body; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.

25:24 And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.

25:25 And the first came out red, all over like a hairy mantle; and they called his name Esav.

25:26 And after that came out his brother, and his hand had hold on Esav's heel; and his name was called Ya'akov. And Yitzhak was sixty years old when she bore them.

25:27 And the boys grew; and Esav was a skillful hunter, a man of the field; and Ya'akov was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.

25:28 Now Yitzhak loved Esav, because he ate of his game; and Rivkah loved Ya'akov.

25:29 And Ya'akov cooked pottage; and Esav came in from the field, and he was faint.

25:30 And Esav said to Ya'akov: Let me swallow, please, some of this red, red pottage; for I am faint. Therefore his name was called Edom.

25:31 And Ya'akov said: Sell me first your birthright.

25:32 And Esav said: Behold, I am about to die; and what profit shall the birthright do to me?

25:33 And Ya'akov said: Swear to me first; and he swore to him; and he sold his birthright to Ya'akov.

25:34 And Ya'akov gave Esav bread and pottage of lentils; and he ate and drank, and rose up, and went his way. So Esav despised his birthright.
